title: Electrical Engineer
description: Electrical Engineer Not Disclosed Mt.Hope/Curepe 20000 - 30000 Permanent full-time Updated 21/11/2026 Human Resource Manager Apply Now Share Share this job Facebook Twitter Report This Job Save Save To ensure the safe, reliable and efficient operation of all plant electrical systems, equipment and machinery through effective planning, supervision and execution of preventative and corrective maintenance, minimizing downtime and supporting production and operational objectives. The Duties and Responsibilities of the Electrical Engineer includes but is not exclusive to the following: Maintenance & Plant Reliability: Plan, schedule and monitor preventative and corrective maintenance activities; troubleshoot electrical faults; maintain accurate maintenance records; monitor equipment condition; and ensure the reliability and availability of electrical machinery, standby generators and the Plant's electrical distribution system. Electrical Systems & Projects: Support electrical installations, upgrades, modifications, commissioning and improvement projects; support and troubleshoot PLC, HMI, drive, servo and industrial network systems; provide technical assistance during breakdowns; and recommend measures to improve equipment reliability, efficiency and safety. Safety & Compliance: Ensure all electrical maintenance activities comply with Company safety rules, applicable legislation, electrical safety standards and established procedures, including appropriate isolation and lockout/tagout practices. Maintain good housekeeping and promote a strong safety culture. Supervision & Staff Development: Supervise electrical maintenance personnel, including attendance, timekeeping, rostering, performance management, training, coaching and development, while ensuring employees have the necessary skills, tools and resources to perform their duties safely and effectively. Tools, Materials & Stores: Ensure the availability and proper condition of tools, testing equipment, spare parts and materials; conduct periodic tool inspections; and liaise with Engineering Stores regarding technical specifications and procurement requirements. Planning, Reporting & Projects: Keep the Plant Engineer/Manager informed of equipment status, maintenance activities, breakdowns and outstanding work; assist with maintenance planning, technical reports, cost estimates and engineering projects; investigate recurring equipment failures and recommend appropriate solutions; and perform other related duties as assigned. QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE Minimum Qualifications Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering from a recognized university. Professional Experience Minimum eight (8) years' experience in electrical maintenance of plant and equipment, preferably within a manufacturing or industrial environment. Minimum five (5) years' experience in a supervisory or leadership capacity. Demonstrated experience in preventative and corrective maintenance of industrial electrical equipment. Experience with electrical distribution systems and standby generators. Demonstrated hands-on experience programming and troubleshooting PLCs, HMIs, variable frequency drives, servo systems and industrial networks within a manufacturing environment. OR An equivalent combination of experience and qualifications. TECHNICAL KNOWLEDGE & COMPETENCIES The successful candidate should possess knowledge and practical experience in: Industrial electrical maintenance. Preventative and predictive maintenance practices. Electrical distribution and protection systems. Standby generators and associated systems. Electrical fault finding and troubleshooting of AC/DC systems and motor control circuits. Motors and starters. Industrial control, automation and networking systems, including industrial communication protocols and cybersecurity awareness. PLC programming, configuration and troubleshooting. HMI development, configuration and support. Variable frequency drives (VFDs). Servo drive and motion control systems. Reading and interpreting electrical drawings and schematics. Maintenance planning and work-order systems. Electrical testing and diagnostic equipment. Workplace electrical safety and safe isolation procedures. Maintenance documentation and reporting. Project implementation and equipment commissioning. CORE SKILLS & COMPETENCIES Excellent verbal and written communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to liaise effectively with employees and stakeholders at all levels. Strong leadership and supervisory skills, including delegation, motivation, coaching, performance management and team development. Strong planning, organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to prioritize maintenance activities based on safety, production requirements and equipment criticality. Strong analytical, troubleshooting and problem-solving skills, with sound technical judgement and decision-making ability. Ability to diagnose electrical faults, identify potential equipment failures and implement appropriate corrective and preventative solutions. Strong attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate maintenance records and documentation. Ability to work effectively under pressure and respond promptly to equipment breakdowns and operational requirements. Commitment to safety, quality, equipment reliability and continuous improvement. Ability and willingness to work flexible hours, including shifts, weekends and call-outs, where operationally required. Proficiency in Microsoft Office and maintenance management systems/software.
